name: Fifty-Fifty Martini
method: Stir with ice until cold, then fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
garnish: Skewered green olive

name: Negroni
method: Add the three ingredients to a rocks glass filled with ice and stir to chill and combine.
garnish: Orange slice or orange zest

name: Margarita on the rocks
method: Shake with ice and strain into a chilled rocks glass over fresh ice.
garnish: Lime wedge; optional salt rim
optional: 6 drops Margarita bitters and 2 drops saline (or a pinch of salt).

name: Gin Rickey
method: Shake the gin, lime and syrup with ice. Strain over fresh ice into a small highball (maximum 300 ml), then add the soda.
garnish: Long lime peel

name: Garibaldi
method: Fine-strain freshly squeezed orange juice and briefly blend without ice to aerate. Stir the Campari, syrup and half the juice over two ice cubes, then add more ice and the remaining juice.
garnish: Orange wedge

name: Gin & It
method: Stir with ice, then fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
garnish: Lemon zest twist

name: White Lady
method: Use pasteurised egg white. Shake all ingredients with ice, strain back into the shaker, shake again without ice, then fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
garnish: Lemon zest twist
optional: 7.5 ml rich sugar syrup, 3 drops saline (or a pinch of salt) and 3 drops orange flower water.

name: Sidecar
method: Shake with ice and fine-strain into a chilled coupe. Add 5 ml chilled water before shaking if using very dry ice; omit it for wet ice.
garnish: Lemon zest twist; sugar rim moistened with orange juice
optional: 2 drops saline or a pinch of salt.

name: Margarita
method: Shake with ice, then fine-strain into a chilled coupe. Serve straight-up, without ice in the glass.
garnish: Lime wedge; optional salt rim

name: Kingston Negroni
method: Use a high-ester overproof pot still rum aged 4–6 years. Stir all ingredients with ice, then strain into a chilled rocks glass over fresh ice.
garnish: Orange slice

name: Boulevardier
method: Stir with ice until chilled, then strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
garnish: Express an orange twist over the drink and add it to the glass.

name: Paper Plane
method: Shake all four ingredients with ice, then fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
garnish: Miniature paper plane clipped to the rim and/or a lemon twist

name: Last Word
method: Shake with ice and fine-strain into a chilled coupe. With ice taken straight from the freezer, include 7.5 ml chilled water; omit the water when using wet ice.
garnish: Express a lime twist over the drink and discard; add skewered maraschino cherries.

name: Vesper
method: Shake all ingredients with ice and fine-strain into a chilled martini glass. Use a blanc quinquina/kina such as Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L’Aéro; dry vermouth is not the specified ingredient.
garnish: Express a lemon twist over the drink and add it to the glass.

name: Old Fashioned
method: Stir all ingredients with ice, then strain into a chilled rocks glass over a large ice cube.
garnish: Express an orange twist over the drink and add it to the glass.

name: Manhattan
method: Use 100-proof (50% ABV) straight rye for Difford’s specified strength. Stir all ingredients with ice and fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
garnish: Express an orange twist over the drink and discard; garnish with a skewered maraschino cherry.

name: Black Manhattan
method: Use 100-proof (50% ABV) straight rye for Difford’s specified strength. Stir with ice and fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
garnish: Maraschino cherry

name: Mai Tai
method: Following Difford’s Trader Vic’s version, use aged Cuban rum (the source specifies Havana Club 7 Años). Shake the five ingredients with ice, then strain into a double rocks glass packed with crushed ice.
garnish: Spent half lime shell, mint sprigs, and skewered pineapple cubes with a maraschino cherry
optional: Float 5 ml dark/black/blackstrap rum on top after straining.

name: Jungle Bird
method: Shake all ingredients with ice, then strain into a chilled rocks glass filled with crushed ice.
garnish: Skewered pineapple wedge and maraschino cherry

name: Sazerac
method: For Difford’s New Orleans-style version, use 100-proof (50% ABV) straight rye. Chill a rocks glass with ice. Separately stir the rye, syrup and Peychaud’s with ice. Empty the serving glass, rinse it with the absinthe, then strain in the cocktail. Serve without ice.
garnish: Express a lemon twist over the drink and use as garnish.

name: Corpse Reviver #2
method: Shake all ingredients with ice and fine-strain into a chilled coupe. This is Difford’s Savoy version, using Lillet Blanc as the aromatised wine.
garnish: Express a lemon twist over the drink and add it to the glass.

name: Mojito
method: Use a light gold column-still rum aged 1–3 years. Add mint, rum, lime and syrup to a chilled Collins glass. Fill two-thirds with crushed ice and churn with a bar spoon. Add more crushed ice, then finish with the soda.
garnish: Bouquet of mint sprigs

name: Americano
method: Pour into a chilled Collins glass filled with ice and give a brief stir.
garnish: Orange slice

name: Whiskey Sour
method: Use pasteurised egg white. Shake all ingredients with ice, strain back into the shaker and shake again without ice. Fine-strain into a chilled rocks glass over fresh ice.
garnish: Skewered lemon slice and maraschino cherry
optional: 2 drops saline or a pinch of salt.

name: Brandy Sour
method: Use cognac and pasteurised egg white. Shake with ice, strain back into the shaker and shake again without ice. Fine-strain over fresh ice in a chilled rocks glass.
garnish: Express a lemon twist and discard; garnish with a skewered lemon slice and maraschino cherry.

name: Aviation (Savoy spec.)
method: Follow the Savoy version, which does not use crème de violette. Shake with ice and fine-strain into a chilled coupe. Include 10 ml chilled water with dry freezer ice; omit it when using wet ice.
garnish: Skewered maraschino cherry; optional sugar rim

name: Southside
method: Gently bruise the mint in a shaker. Add gin, lime and syrup, then shake with ice and fine-strain into a chilled coupe. If using the optional soda, add it after straining.
garnish: Mint leaf
optional: 2 drops saline (or a tiny pinch of salt) and 10 ml chilled soda water.

name: Mint Julep
method: Chill the serving cup well. Gently bruise the mint in a shaker, add the other ingredients and shake with ice. Fine-strain into the cup packed with crushed ice.
garnish: Mint sprigs dusted with icing sugar

name: Tommy’s Margarita
method: Shake with ice, then fine-strain over fresh ice in a chilled rocks glass.
garnish: Lime wedge

name: John Collins
method: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice. Open the shaker and add the chilled soda without shaking again, then strain into a chilled Collins glass over fresh ice. This is Difford’s London dry gin Collins; its Tom Collins uses old tom gin.
garnish: Skewered lemon slice and maraschino cherry

name: Dry Martini (5:1)
method: Use gin chilled in the freezer and refrigerated vermouth. Stir with ice, then fine-strain into a chilled martini glass.
garnish: Chilled green olive and/or expressed lemon twist; may also be served without garnish

name: Silver Gin Fizz
method: Use pasteurised egg white. Shake everything except soda with ice, strain back into the shaker and shake again without ice. Fine-strain into a chilled small highball with no ice. Rest in the freezer for about a minute to set the foam, then slowly add chilled soda to lift the head.
garnish: Quarter lemon slice
